name: Biggest (point-in-time)
description: At each year-end close, buy the point-in-time S&P 500 constituent with the largest approximated market cap, and hold that single name until the next year-end close.
signal: approximated market cap at the prior year-end close

data_source.label: Yahoo Finance free daily prices
data_source.banner: POINT-IN-TIME ATTEMPT — free prices, Wikipedia selected changes. Not a complete survivorship-bias-free universe: the changes table is thin before ~2011, and names Yahoo and Stooq cannot price are logged. Sharadar (SEP / SF1 / TICKERS) is the exact source.

universe.source: wikipedia:List of S&P 500 companies + Historical components selected changes
universe.note: Membership is today's S&P 500 walked back through Wikipedia's selected-changes table (Historical components of the S&P 500, linked from List of S&P 500 companies). The table records 411 changes (62 of them before 2011). Years with only a handful of rows are only partly point-in-time. Sharadar TICKERS is the complete membership file.
universe.description: At each year-end close, buy the point-in-time S&P 500 constituent with the largest approximated market cap, and hold that single name until the next year-end close.

market_cap_note: Historical market cap on the free source is an approximation: split-adjusted close × the nearest Yahoo share count, multiplied by splits that occurred after that share-count date. Dates before Yahoo's first share record use the earliest record. Names with no share history use today's share count. Buybacks, issuance, and stale records are not corrected. Sharadar SF1 marketcap replaces this.
caveats: SURVIVORSHIP-BIASED — free Yahoo Finance source. The universe is the current S&P 500, not point-in-time membership. A survivorship-bias-free universe requires Sharadar (SEP / SF1 / TICKERS).
Prices are Yahoo's daily bars. Adjusted closes (Adj Close) include splits and dividends. Traded closes (Close) are split-adjusted only and are what the market-cap approximation multiplies by shares.

Historical market cap ≈ nearest reported shares × later splits × split-adjusted close. If Yahoo has no share history, today's share count is used instead. This is not point-in-time. Sharadar SF1 marketcap replaces it.
Rebalance is the year-end close. The signal uses only prices through that close. The fill is that same close, which is a small optimistic bias versus trading the next open.
Equal weight. Dividends enter through adjusted closes: the book holds a constant share count of the adjusted series, which matches total return.

Sharadar SF1 marketcap replaces this.
warnings: Stooq answered with a browser check instead of a CSV, so it filled no delisted names on this run. Unpriceable tickers are listed on the book.
19 removed tickers had no Yahoo/Stooq prints during a membership spell (often a recycled symbol, or a delisted name Yahoo no longer stores): ADT, APC, BBBY, CAM, CSRA, EMC, INFO, NE, …
12 names used today's share count (no Yahoo share history): KFT, ACE, TYC, BMS, KFT, ACE, TYC, BMS, …
